# pengdows.efcore.conformance

> Black-box conformance tests for relational providers of Entity Framework Core 10.

## Purpose

This repository tests externally observable behavior through documented EF Core public APIs. The provider is configured through an adapter, operations run through `DbContext`, LINQ, and EF Core relational APIs, and results are asserted through fresh contexts or documented public state.

## Boundary

- Do not inspect generated SQL, EF provider services, EF internals, or provider implementation types in shared tests.
- Keep provider setup and database provisioning in `IProviderAdapter` implementations.
- Capabilities declare applicability only. They never alter expected values or assertions.
- Strict runs require a supported or unsupported declaration for every feature in `ProviderCapabilities.KnownFeatures`.
- ADO.NET `DataTypes` metadata is the preferred native type inventory. Mark catalog evidence independent only when it is independent of the EF model. Types read from test-created tables are `SELF_DERIVED` and excluded from coverage totals.
- Npgsql independently inventories PostgreSQL types from public `pg_type` and `pg_namespace`; scalar name comparison is scoped to `pg_catalog` while full catalog metadata from other schemas is retained. A live PostgreSQL 17 check found 469 `pg_catalog` names, 133 ADO.NET rows, 53 exact matches, 75 normalized alias matches, 341 catalog-only names, and five ADO.NET-only `information_schema` pseudo-domain names. Pomelo reads MySQL system-schema columns from `information_schema.COLUMNS`; a live MySQL 8.4 check found 3,551 catalog columns across 23 distinct observed type families and 51 ADO.NET metadata rows. This is an observed system-catalog column inventory, not an exhaustive MySQL type list. Catalog differences are discovery evidence, not automatic EF mapping failures or generated EF mapping coverage.
- Run the same test assembly against one provider per process. Compare report JSON with the runner's `--compare` command.

## Project map

- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Contracts/`: adapter contracts, capabilities, type discovery, and outcomes.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner/`: adapter loading, test execution, JSON/JUnit reports, type discovery, and cross-provider comparison.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Inventory/`: reflection-generated EF Core public API inventory.
- `tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/`: shared EF Core 10 relational behavioral tests.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/`: Microsoft provider reference adapter; included in the standalone solution.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.PengdowsSqlite/`: pengdows adapter; depends on the separate pengdows ADO.NET repository and is intentionally outside the solution build.
- `manifests/`: EF Core 10 contract and generated API inventory.

## Build and run

```sh
dotnet build pengdows.efcore.conformance.slnx
export PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING='Data Source=/tmp/efcore-reference.db'
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --run \
  tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational.csproj \
  "$PWD/adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/bin/Debug/net10.0/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.dll" \
  pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.MicrosoftSqliteAdapter /tmp/efcore-reference-report
```

Run the same test assembly for another provider with a separate disposable database and report directory. Compare results:

```sh
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --compare \
  /tmp/candidate-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/efcore-reference-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/provider-comparison.json
```

Append `--cleanup-database` to `--run` only when the configured database is dedicated and disposable. The runner then calls the adapter cleanup hook after writing test results.

## Provider configuration

The sibling ADO.NET conformance project uses `providers/*.json` profiles to describe driver, target, connection string, environment, dialect, and type inventory. The EF Core harness borrows declarative per-provider profiles for adapter selection and connection strings: `profiles/*.json` names a compiled adapter assembly/type and a connection string template with `${ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE}` placeholders. Run one with `--run-profile <profile.json> <test-project> <report-directory> [--cleanup-database]`. Adapter assembly paths are relative to the profile file unless absolute.

EF profiles deliberately leave EF provider configuration, capabilities, database initialization, and cleanup in `IProviderAdapter`. A profile cannot change expectations or assertions. Profiles do not provision containers or remote databases; infrastructure setup remains external. The old direct `--run` form and `PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING` are still supported.

## Current status

- EF Core baseline: 10.0.14 on `net10.0`.
- The public API inventory is generated from the Core, Abstractions, Relational, and Design assemblies. Disposition rules in `manifests/efcore-10.json` attach rationales to EF-owned and provider-service surfaces; tests override those rules. Current counts: 18,795 entries, 780 overload entries linked to runtime behavioral families, 0 uncovered member families, 0 entries awaiting classification, 3,532 EF-owned entries, and 8,357 provider-service or model-configuration entries marked not directly applicable. Applicable Design behavior is tested; remaining tooling and dependency wiring has explicit provider-applicability rationales.
- Provider reports exclude harness-only type discovery and catalog comparer tests (trait `Category=HarnessUnit`); run these six test cases separately with `dotnet test ... --filter Category=HarnessUnit`. Latest full provider runs: Microsoft SQLite 368 pass / 5 fail / 21 unsupported across 394 cases; Pomelo MySQL 629 / 5 / 12 across 646 cases; Npgsql PostgreSQL 1,140 / 35 / 1 across 1,176 cases. The last pengdows SQLite run used the prior 350-case assembly (319 / 10 / 21); two caller-owned connection cases, two reader command-interception cases, two command-parameter rewriting cases, two materialization-interception cases, two connection open/close interception cases, two connection disposal interception cases, two non-query command-interception cases, two transaction begin/commit cases, two transaction rollback cases, two savepoint rollback cases, two savepoint release cases, two save suppression cases, two query-compilation interceptor cases, two integer-boundary fidelity cases, four DateTime/DateTimeOffset temporal round-trip cases, and four `DbSet` range add/update/remove cases, and eight `Distinct`, `Union`, `Intersect`, and `Except` sync/async cases have since passed on Microsoft SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL; temporal checks also cover predicates, six-digit precision boundaries, and nullable insert/update-to-null. DateTimeKind and non-UTC offset preservation are not asserted where the database type stores an instant only. Each provider run includes passing public EF Design scenarios for migration code generation/scaffolding and reverse-engineering model helpers. MySQL includes 260 generated native-type insert/read/update/null/parameter-query cases; PostgreSQL includes 790. Each type case inserts through EF Core and reads through a fresh context. Each native mapping has its own EF model and generated table setup so one unsupported mapping cannot turn unrelated tests into infrastructure failures. The external-connection ownership tests confirm sync/async context disposal leaves caller-owned connections open. Command interceptor tests verify sync and async reader and non-query callbacks, public ADO.NET bound-parameter rewriting, and duplicate-key command-failure callbacks; materialization interceptor tests verify ordered entity construction callbacks; connection interceptor tests verify creation, sync/async open and close, and disposal notifications; transaction interceptors verify sync/async begin, commit, rollback, externally enlisted transaction use, savepoint rollback, and release callbacks with persistence checked through fresh contexts. SaveChanges suppression cases assert a zero affected count and confirm no row persisted; query-compilation callbacks preserve ordinary query results. Five failures (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched-row `RightJoin`, and sync/async TPT save counts) reproduce on all providers. Five decimal fidelity failures are pengdows-only. PostgreSQL also fails sync/async `Least`/`Greatest` translation, sync/async `tsquery` parameter equality, and mapping fidelity for `oidvector`, `int2vector`, and their array forms; `regconfig` parameter equality fails too. Reference-provider failures support triage but do not prove an EF Core defect.
- Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 and Npgsql/PostgreSQL 17 adapters have profiles. MySQL passes 629/646 cases, including all 260 generated native-type insert/read/update/null/parameter-query cases, with five shared failures and 12 explicit unsupported results. PostgreSQL passes 1,140/1,176 cases, including 790 generated native-type scenarios; 35 cases fail and one is explicitly unsupported. The failures are five shared cases, two `Least`/`Greatest` translations, two `tsquery` parameterized equality queries, 24 cases across four native mapping declarations, and two `regconfig` parameterized equality cases. SQLite declares ambient `System.Transactions` and independent native-type discovery unsupported, while MySQL passes sync and async enlistment. Both SQLite adapters pass sync/async `ReferentialAction.SetDefault` migration tests. Database-collation migration passes on Pomelo MySQL and is unsupported on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
- Independent ADO.NET type discovery now drives per-type tests from the adapter's declarative CLR/store-type mapping profile. MySQL Connector reports 51 metadata rows / 41 native names; 33 type/mapping rows pass generated sync/async insert/read/update/null/parameter-query fidelity and 13 are unlinked. Npgsql reports 133 types including arrays, ranges, multiranges, geometric, and full-text types; 110 type rows pass, six fail, and 17 are unlinked. The profile exercises transaction-ID arrays, range arrays, geometric values, full-text values, `bytea[]`, catalog vectors, and registry types. `oidvector` and `int2vector` fail mapping tests; their metadata-derived array forms fail independently. Run outputs place actual outcomes in `ado-net-types.json`. `UNLINKED` means the adapter does not claim a mapping; it is not a provider failure. SQLite does not advertise `DataTypes`, so its supplemental test-schema evidence is self-derived and excluded from independent coverage.
- SQLite ADO.NET providers do not advertise `DataTypes`. Supplemental types discovered from test-created schema are self-derived; independent native type coverage is not currently established for SQLite.
- Public type declarations, compiler-generated enum backing fields, and inherited `System.Object` overrides carry explicit non-applicability rationales because they are inventory nodes or EF-owned object behavior rather than provider operations. The test suite is a growing conformance slice, not yet complete coverage of every applicable EF Core public API. Consult `README.md`, `manifests/efcore-10.json`, and `manifests/efcore-10-api-inventory.json` for disposition rules, current counts, rationales, and uncovered members.


## Unfinished work

Inventory dimensions overlap: uncovered member families are distinct from APIs given explicit non-applicability rationales.

1. Classification: the Core, Abstractions, Relational, and Design inventories now have zero unclassified entries and zero uncovered member families. Reverse-engineering helpers and migration generator/scaffolder output have behavioral links; provider dependency bags, project file removal, and bundle entry points have explicit black-box applicability rationales. Review those rationales as EF contracts evolve. PostgreSQL exercises sequence, schema, and schema-qualified function APIs; database-collation migration is unsupported on PostgreSQL and SQLite. `MigrationBuilder` operation-list construction and inspection are excluded as EF-owned in-memory behavior.
2. Expand behavioral matrices across all families. Add overload, boundary, failure, composition, and interaction cases; run sync and async paths independently. Linkage alone does not mean an overload or scenario executed.
3. Triage the five pengdows-only decimal fidelity failures, the five failures reproduced across all four providers (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched `RightJoin`, sync/async TPT save counts), and 30 PostgreSQL-only failures (sync/async `Least`/`Greatest`, sync/async parameterized `tsquery` equality, 24 cases across `oidvector`, `int2vector`, and their arrays, and sync/async `regconfig` parameter equality) against documented contracts. Reproduction on a reference provider is evidence, not proof of an EF Core defect.
4. Expand native-type fidelity. MySQL and PostgreSQL generate sync/async insert, fresh-context retrieval, update, null, and applicable scalar parameter-query tests for declared mappings. Continue adding boundary-value and type-specific query scenarios and expand profiles where EF has a public mapping. PostgreSQL has a `pg_catalog` inventory comparison; MySQL has a bounded inventory from system-schema columns. Add independent catalogs for other providers where the database exposes one.
5. Expand beyond the first Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 run to additional relational providers and server versions, keeping shared expectations provider-independent and capability declarations explicit.
6. Add a separate EF Core 11 target after its release contract is established; generate its inventory from its actual assemblies and add version-specific tests for changed or new behavior.

EF Core 10 completion requires zero unclassified entries, behavioral or justified disposition for each applicable public API family, sync/async coverage where both APIs exist, independently discovered native-type coverage, triaged failures, and reports that distinguish pass, fail, unsupported, infrastructure error, and uncovered work. Current full provider runs cover 394 Microsoft SQLite, 646 MySQL, and 1,176 PostgreSQL cases; six harness unit-test cases run separately. Every inventoried Design member now has a test link or an explicit applicability rationale; review those rationales as EF contracts evolve. Native-type boundary values, richer type-specific query operations, independent catalogs beyond MySQL and PostgreSQL, and the remaining API scenario matrices still need work.
